Routing notes:
- Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office, D external partner.
- Confirmed successful route:
  - Large claim, south region, requester says client has asked twice → B (REQ-2400).
  - Small shipment, north region, “second attempt, first form bounced” → C (REQ-2408).
- Rejections:
  - C was invalid for large refund/south, small claim/north, large shipment/east, small shipment/east, large claim/south, and large refund/east.
  - B was invalid for small claim/north and large refund/south.
- Do not infer that urgency/repeated attempts alone determine the route; the same “asked twice” note led to B for a large claim/south but B failed for a large refund/south and small claim/north.
- Do not assume regional office (C) is correct merely because the request came through or concerns a region; most C selections failed, with only the small shipment/north second-attempt case confirmed.
- No evidence yet for A or D.

Routing notes:
- Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office, D external partner.
- Confirmed successful routes:
  - B: large claim, south; requester says client asked twice (REQ-2400).
  - C: small shipment, north; “second attempt, first form bounced” (REQ-2408).
  - A: small claim/east (“same as last month”), large claim/east (regional-office submission; REQ-2413, REQ-2415), large shipment/south (“no rush”), small claim/south, and small shipment/south (second attempt; REQ-2410, REQ-2416, REQ-2418, REQ-2419).
- Rejections:
  - A: large invoice/north and small shipment/east.
  - B: small claim/north, large refund/south, and large invoice/east.
  - C: large refund/south, small claim/north, large shipment/east, small shipment/east, large claim/south, and large refund/east.
  - D: large shipment/north.
- Do not infer route from urgency, repeated attempts, or regional-office origin alone. Similar notes have produced different routes.
- A is now supported for several claim/shipment cases, especially south-region examples, but is not valid for every request (known failures: large invoice/north, small shipment/east).
- C remains weakly supported: only the small shipment/north second-attempt case is confirmed; most observed C selections failed.
- B is confirmed only for the large claim/south case and failed for several other request types.
- No successful D route yet.

Routing notes:
- Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office, D external partner.
- Confirmed successful routes:
  - A: small claim/east (“same as last month”), large claim/east (regional-office submission; REQ-2413, REQ-2415), large shipment/south (“no rush”), small claim/south, small shipment/south (second attempt; REQ-2410, REQ-2416, REQ-2418, REQ-2419).
  - B: large claim/south, client asked twice (REQ-2400). However, B failed for the same large claim/south type with “same as last month” notes (REQ-2422, REQ-2426), so do not generalize.
  - C: small shipment/north, second attempt/first form bounced (REQ-2408). No other confirmed C successes.
  - D: small claim/north (“no rush”; REQ-2420), small invoice/east (“let me know if anything is missing”; REQ-2423), large claim/north (scanned paperwork; REQ-2429).
- Rejections:
  - A: large invoice/north, small shipment/east, small refund/east (scanned paperwork).
  - B: small claim/north, large refund/south, large invoice/east, large shipment/north, and large claim/south when note says “same as last month.”
  - C: large refund/south, small claim/north, large shipment/east, small shipment/east, large claim/south, large refund/east.
  - D: large shipment/north, large refund/north, small invoice/east when client asked twice, and small shipment/east on second attempt.
- Do not infer route from urgency, repeated attempts, regional-office origin, sender, or paperwork format alone; identical request types can route differently based on note/context.
- A is supported for several claim/shipment cases but has known failures. D now has several successes but is also context-sensitive. No reliable universal route pattern yet.

Routing notes:
- Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office, D external partner.
- Confirmed successes:
  - A: small claim/east (“same as last month”); large claim/east (regional-office submission; REQ-2413, REQ-2415); large shipment/east (“no rush”); large shipment/south (“no rush”); small claim/south (scanned paperwork and “no rush”); small shipment/south (second attempt; REQ-2410, REQ-2416, REQ-2418, REQ-2419); small invoice/south (“same as last month”; REQ-2438).
  - B: large claim/south when client asked twice (REQ-2400); small shipment/east with end-of-day urgency (REQ-2431). B failed for large claim/south with “same as last month” (REQ-2422, REQ-2426), so do not generalize.
  - C: small shipment/north, second attempt/first form bounced (REQ-2408). No other confirmed C successes.
  - D: small claim/north (“no rush”; REQ-2420); small invoice/east (“let me know if anything is missing”; REQ-2423); large claim/north (scanned paperwork; REQ-2429); small claim/south (scanned paperwork; REQ-2432).
- New rejections:
  - A: large invoice/north; small shipment/east; small refund/east (scanned); small refund/north (“no rush”).
  - B: prior failures plus none newly rejected.
  - C: large refund/south; small claim/north; large shipment/east; small shipment/east; large claim/south; large refund/east.
  - D: large shipment/north; large refund/north; small invoice/east when client asked twice; small shipment/east on second attempt; large invoice/north; small invoice/north; large invoice/east.
- No reliable universal route. Do not infer from urgency, attempts, region-office origin, sender, or paperwork format alone. Context matters; A now covers several invoice/claim/shipment cases but has failures, while D is successful for some scanned claims yet fails multiple invoice cases.

Routing notes:
- Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office, D external partner.
- Confirmed successes:
  - A: small claim/east; large claim/east via regional-office submission (REQ-2413, REQ-2415); large shipment/east and south (“no rush”); small claim/south scanned/no rush; small shipment/south (second attempt; REQ-2410, REQ-2416, REQ-2418, REQ-2419); small invoice/south; small and large invoice/south with scanned paperwork (REQ-2448, REQ-2449).
  - B: large claim/south when client asked twice (REQ-2400); small shipment/east with urgency or “missing” note (REQ-2431, REQ-2440, REQ-2446); large invoice/east (“no rush” or regional-office origin; REQ-2442, REQ-2447).
  - C: small shipment/north, second attempt after first form bounced (REQ-2408). No other confirmed successes.
  - D: small claim/north; small invoice/east with “missing” note; large claim/north scanned; small claim/south scanned (REQ-2420, REQ-2423, REQ-2429, REQ-2432).
- Important failures:
  - A rejected large shipment/east when submitted as coming through regional office (REQ-2441), despite an earlier success for large shipment/east/no rush.
  - B failed large claim/south with “same as last month”; small shipment/south with urgency; large shipment/north even when asked twice (REQ-2444); retain prior failures.
  - D failed large claim/south with scanned paperwork (REQ-2445), so scanned format is not sufficient.
  - C has repeated failures across regions/types; avoid unless matching the narrow small-shipment/north case.
- No universal route. Do not infer from urgency, attempts, region-office origin, sender, or paperwork format alone. Context and request type/region combinations matter.

Routing notes:
- Options: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office, D external partner.
- Confirmed successes:
  - A: small claim/east; large claim/east when submitted through regional office (REQ-2413, REQ-2415, REQ-2450, REQ-2455); large shipment/east and south (“no rush”); small claim/south scanned/no rush; small shipment/south on second attempt; small invoice/south; small/large invoice/south with scanned paperwork.
  - B: large claim/south when client asked twice (REQ-2400, REQ-2459); small shipment/east with urgency or “missing” note; large invoice/east with “no rush” or regional-office origin (REQ-2442, REQ-2447, REQ-2457).
  - C: only small shipment/north on second attempt after first form bounced (REQ-2408).
  - D: small claim/north; small invoice/east with “missing”; large claim/north with “missing” note (REQ-2453); large claim/north scanned; small claim/south scanned (REQ-2420, REQ-2423, REQ-2429, REQ-2432).
- Important failures:
  - A: large shipment/east via regional office (REQ-2441); large refund/east when client asked twice (REQ-2451); large shipment/north on second attempt (REQ-2458).
  - B: large claim/south with “same as last month”; small shipment/south with urgency; large shipment/north even when asked twice; small refund/east with urgency (REQ-2456).
  - D: small claim/south scanned (REQ-2452); small refund/north scanned (REQ-2454); large claim/south scanned (REQ-2445).
  - C has repeated failures; avoid except narrow small-shipment/north case.
- No universal route. Match request type, region, note, attempt status, and paperwork; do not rely on urgency, sender, regional-office origin, or scanned format alone. Refund patterns remain sparse and should not be generalized.
